correctness.rationale: For c=a/(a+b), 1<=a<b coprime, the allowed transition after a one is governed by integer height H=aN0−bN1; zeros add a, ones subtract b. Legal zero states have a free zero (+a) and whenever h<b the legal block 10 (−(b−a)); lowering h>=b with a chosen one and finitely many forced ones reaches h<b. Since gcd(a,b−a)=1, any integer zero state connects to any other by blocks 10 followed by zeros, including reachable states from an initial zero. This gives a bridge from any finite language factor u to v via zero-state communication, proving topological transitivity. Construct ω=1 0^m 1^r 0 with am≡1 (mod b), am>b, r=(am−1)/b+1; its initial forced zero and final long 1-run respectively impose h<=b−1 and h>=b−1. Every occurrence therefore starts at exactly h=b−1 and all pairwise returns have zero discrepancy, hence lengths divisible by a+b, excluding mixing. Independent finite transition replay verified unique marker start for six coprime pairs; infinite statement rests on Bezout and height argument.

The new combined transitive/nonmixing classification is not subsumed by these.
